omar.s: hey all — married partner but not legally married in the US. My partner lives in Mexico and doesn't have a US SSN. Can I add them as a domestic partner to my benefits? What docs do you need and will premiums be pre-tax?

lina: short answer: possibly. Domestic partner rules depend on the plan and tax treatment depends on federal rules (imputed income). We'll need partner proof + tax form.

benefits-ops: requirements: 1) completed Affidavit of Domestic Partnership (signed) 2) proof of shared residence or financial interdependence (utility, lease, joint bank) 3) partner ID (passport) and translation if not English. If no SSN, enroll as SSN pending and upload paperwork when available.

legal: tax note: if the partner is not a tax dependent under IRS rules, the value of employer-paid benefits is considered imputed income and will be taxed. We can provide an estimate of imputed income. If they qualify as a tax dependent, premiums may be pre-tax. You should consult a tax advisor.

payroll-bot: payroll: mark dependent as "domestic partner (intl)" in Workday. If imputed income applies, you'll see additional taxable withholding on the next payroll after enrollment (we'll notify before posting). If SSN arrives later, update Workday to avoid penalties.

omar.s: thanks — timeline? I need cover starting 2026-09-01 for upcoming surgery.

benefits-ops: upload docs today; we'll submit an admin enrollment request requesting effective 2026-09-01. Carrier approval and tax review may take up to 10 business days. We'll flag urgent medical need on the ticket.

omar.s: got it — uploading affidavit now. Appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
